newsitem.title: USA: NYS keeps Food Stamps for some immigrants -- paper.
newsitem.headline: NYS keeps Food Stamps for some immigrants -- paper.

text.p: New York State's new fiscal 1998 budget keeps Food Stamps for some legal immigrants who were living in the state before the federal welfare law went into effect last August, Newsday said in its Tuesday edition.

The provision, which covers immigrants who are under 18 years of age, elderly or disabled, was expected to protect about 67,000 of the 147,000 legal immigrants who would have lost Food Stamps, according to the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, a Washington-based think tank.
The paper said the budget sets aside $19.8 million in combined state and local money for Food Stamps, and earmarks another $13 million New York gets in a federal welfare block grant for the program.

Local service districts must opt to participate, Newsday said, citing the budget bill. It added that New York City, where the vast majority of the state's legal immigrants live, was expected to join the program.

Further, immigrants must have lived in the district in which they applied for Food Stamps as of August 22, 1996, when the new federal rules went into effect. And they must apply for citizenship within 30 days of becoming eligible to do so.

New York State's new budget also would give legal immigrants who arrive after the bill goes into effect with one year of noncash benefits under the state's safety net program, before they get their lifetime limit of two years of cash benefits, the paper said, quoting Dan Hogan, of the state Department of Social Services.
